Its core method uses internal neuron activations to intelligently select training data and construct a teacher model for self-distillation. This approach aims to improve LLM performance in specialized domains without costly human annotations, overcoming limitations of previous annotation-free methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the Proposed Neuron-OPSD.

top_papers.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a simple, real-time online safety monitor for LLMs. It leverages an external verifier model's signal and calibrates a threshold based on risk control to trigger alarms when safety is compromised. The core contribution is demonstrating that this straightforward thresholding approach is competitive with more complex sequential testing methods for detecting unsafe LLM outputs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Monitoring factuality on mathematical reasoning (MATH): CRC and UCB calibrate a single threshold to turn a PRM score into an alarm, yet detect incorrect answers earlier ( third row ) than e-valuators, which train several density estimators.

top_papers.title: Reasoning effort, not tool access, buys first-try reliability in agentic code generation: an observational study
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether increased capabilities or reasoning effort improves agentic code generation. Through an observational study of 90 agent runs building the same application, they found that **model generation (capability tier) was the primary driver of first-try reliability, not tool access or prompt design.** Their contribution lies in demonstrating that **frontier models significantly outperform older ones, and that specific complex tasks like container deployment remain challenging and inconsistently reliable across different agent configurations.**

top_papers.title: Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a "constrained substrate" approach for scalable oversight of coding agents, drawing parallels to traditional software engineering practices like access control and coding conventions. By imposing these constraints, the system significantly improves the ability of a small reviewer agent to detect security vulnerabilities (backdoors) in a Python codebase, demonstrating a substantial increase in recall compared to unconstrained agents. The core contribution lies in showing that established engineering principles are a cost-effective and scalable method for managing AI coding agents, outperforming more complex agentic scaffolding.

top_papers.title: VisionAId: An Offline-First Multimodal Android Assistant for People with Visual Impairment, Featuring Personalized Object Retrieval
top_papers.abstract: VisionAId is an Android app that transforms a smartphone into an offline-first visual assistant for the visually impaired. Its core method integrates multiple on-device deep learning models for real-time object recognition, depth estimation, and face detection, with an optional cloud LLM for enhanced descriptions. A key contribution is its few-shot learning capability, allowing users to personalize object retrieval by simply photographing their belongings.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overall layered architecture of VisionAId. All perception runs on-device; the cloud language model is an optional component used only for narrative scene description and object labeling.

top_papers.title: WorldSample: Closed-loop Real-robot RL with World Modelling
top_papers.abstract: WorldSample addresses the high cost of real-world reinforcement learning (RL) for robots by creating a closed loop between physical interactions and a learned world model. It uses real robot data to train a high-fidelity world model, which then generates synthetic transitions to augment training. This approach, combined with a novel Policy-Paced Learning strategy for sample selection, significantly reduces the need for costly physical rollouts while improving policy performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: WorldSample overview. WorldSample expands real-robot rollout into multiple physically grounded synthetic trajectories with an action-conditioned world model, forming a real-synthetic training loop that improves success rate and reduces interaction cost.

top_papers.title: Bringing Agentic Search to Earth Observation Data Discovery
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces an agentic search system that leverages NASA's Earth Observation Knowledge Graph to improve discovery of geoscience data and tools. By combining a neural scorer fine-tuned on a new benchmark with BM25 and a zero-shot agentic reranking stage, the system significantly enhances search relevance and recall for natural language queries. The core contribution is demonstrating how agentic search amplifies the value of knowledge graphs for complex data discovery.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the three-stage agentic search pipeline (Section 5.1 ). Stage 1 : the Router first attempts to resolve each query via NASA official tools (Harmony, SDE, WorldView, Giovanni); queries that can be fully answered here terminate early. Stage 2 : if no official tool suffices, the hybrid BM25 + NN-SSC retriever surfaces the most relevant datasets from the NASA CMR corpus. Stage 3 : retrieved candidates are reranked by an LLM that autonomously invokes web search and arXiv paper lookup to ground its ranking decisions in external context; the final ranked list is returned to the user.

top_papers.title: DecompRL: Solving Harder Problems by Learning Modular Code Generation
top_papers.abstract: DecompRL addresses the limitations of LLMs in solving complex problems by learning to decompose them into smaller, independently solvable sub-functions. Instead of brute-force sampling or relying solely on gradient signals, this RL algorithm explicitly learns to generate and recombine modular code structures. This approach significantly expands the search space of potential solutions by combining implementations of different modules, enabling LLMs to tackle problems previously beyond their capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Decomp RL solves harder problems than existing RL methods. Our hierarchical training learns 1) a decomposition policy that breaks down problems into simpler functions and 2) an implementation policy that writes code for each function in parallel. Given a high token budget, Decomp RL solves up to 35 % 35\% problems of the LiveCodeBench hard subset ( 2024 / 08 / 01 2024/08/01 to 2025 / 02 / 01 2025/02/01 ) Jain et al. ( 2024a ) .

top_papers.title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-II: Representational Similarity Observatory
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces TGO-II, a framework for analyzing the geometric evolution of Vision Transformer representations during training. Using methods like CKA and SVCCA, it reveals that representational similarity decreases as training progresses, indicating increasing specialization of internal features. This work contributes a novel approach to understanding the internal dynamics of Vision Transformers beyond just attention mechanisms.

top_papers.title: WattGPU: Predicting Inference Power and Latency on Unseen GPUs and LLMs
top_papers.abstract: WattGPU introduces two predictive models that estimate LLM inference power and latency using only publicly available LLM metadata and GPU specifications. This novel approach eliminates the need for hardware profiling, enabling accurate predictions for unseen GPUs and LLMs. The core contribution is a generalized, hardware-agnostic prediction system for optimizing LLM deployments.
top_papers.figure_caption: GPU selection is a key lever for energy savings in LLM inference. For deploying Llama 3.1 8B with a Service Level Agreement (SLA) of a mean ITL < 25 <25 ms, it is possible to reduce power draw by 43% by choosing an A30 instead of an H100. Data from the Watt Counts dataset showing only GPUs where the LLM fits in memory.

top_papers.title: The Future of NLP may not be at NLP Conferences: Scholarly Migration Patterns in Natural Language Processing
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates scholarly migration patterns in NLP, finding that the field's center of gravity is shifting away from traditional NLP conferences like ACL. The core method involves analyzing publication trends of both established and new authors, comparing pre- and post-LLM eras. The key contribution is demonstrating a significant migration of NLP research to general ML venues and newer "Findings" tracks, indicating a blurring of disciplinary boundaries due to LLM advancements.
top_papers.figure_caption: Per-year mean share of papers at each of the three tracked venue families per cohort author, renormalized to sum to one (topic-active cohort, N = 4 , 181 N=4{,}181 ). The cohort’s *ACL share holds near 76–80% through 2020 and then declines to 63% by 2025; General-ML rises monotonically from ∼ \( \sim \) 4% in 2015 to 31% in 2025, overtaking AI-Broad (which falls from 19% to 7%) around 2022–2023.

top_papers.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates if scaling up Large Language Models (LLMs) improves their fidelity in social simulations. The core method involves training and evaluating LLMs under varying compute budgets and parameter sizes across opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, and longitudinal forecasting. The key contribution is the surprising finding that **compute scaling significantly improves social simulation fidelity**, suggesting that current scaling trends are beneficial for this application.
top_papers.figure_caption: Compute Scaling Laws. We observe log-linear improvements in task loss on all three social science tasks after scaling compute alone with models trained on DCLM (Li et al. , 2024 ) from 10 18 10^{18} to 10 20 10^{20} FLOPs.

top_papers.title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
top_papers.abstract: Cortex addresses the limitations of current embodied agents in long-horizon manipulation by bridging the gap between high-level planning and low-level execution. Its core method involves a novel planning interface that translates semantic plans from a Vision-Language Model into executable subtasks for a Vision-Language-Action model. The key contribution is the standardization of manipulation into 32 skill primitives and the injection of tractability principles during data generation, enabling efficient training on extensive real-world and simulated data.
top_papers.figure_caption: Compared to previous works, Cortex is an embodied agent framework aligning the high-level VLM and low-level VLA on the subtask executability and tractability, enabling synergistic planning and execution for long-horizon manipulation.

top_papers.title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness For Variational Automation Tasks
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Graph-as-Policy (GaP), a novel multi-agent self-learning harness for variational automation tasks. GaP generates directed computation graphs from a modular skill library, which are then iteratively refined through parallel simulations to improve reliability in complex, open-world robotic applications. Its core contribution lies in bridging interpretable robot programming with the adaptability of model-free policies for tasks with significant object variations.

top_papers.title: MoP-JEPA: Hard-Assigned Predictor Mixtures for Stochastic JEPA World Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MoP-JEPA, a novel approach to world modeling for stochastic environments. Unlike traditional JEPA models that use a single predictor leading to collapsed predictions, MoP-JEPA employs hard-assigned predictor mixtures. This allows the model to learn a quantizer of the transition distribution, with each predictor head representing a distinct successor state mode, significantly improving planning performance on complex tasks.

top_papers.title: Multiplayer Interactive World Models with Representation Autoencoders
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the first multiplayer world model capable of simulating complex, dynamic environments by conditioning on the actions of multiple agents. Its core method uses a large latent diffusion model to learn how to attribute scene changes to specific players and maintain coherence under arbitrary action combinations. The key contribution is enabling realistic, real-time generation of multi-agent interactions, demonstrated in Rocket League, with stable long-term rollouts exceeding training horizons.

top_papers.title: OptiAgent: End-to-End Optimization Modeling via Multi-Agent Iterative Refinement
top_papers.abstract: OptiAgent is a multi-agent framework that translates natural language descriptions of optimization problems into solver-ready mathematical formulations and executable code. Its core method involves dedicated agents iteratively refining the model through a novel multi-loop validation architecture that addresses various failure modes. The main contribution is an end-to-end, auditable optimization modeling process that achieves state-of-the-art performance on LP, MILP, and Nonlinear Programming tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: OptiAgent: a multi-agent framework with internal feedback loops for iterative refinement of the optimization formulation and generated code.

top_papers.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Hierarchical Vocabulary Routing (HeRo), a novel watermarking method for LLMs that enables selective disclosure of embedded metadata. Unlike previous methods, HeRo allows different verifiers to access only specific parts of the watermark based on their authorization level, enhancing privacy and controlling information exposure. This is achieved by recursively partitioning the vocabulary and distributing watermark information hierarchically.
top_papers.figure_caption: Hierarchical vocabulary routing on a toy vocabulary of size V = 16 V=16 with a chunking schedule K = ( K 1 ) = ( 4 ) K=(K_{1})=(4) . At stage ℓ = 1 \( \ell \)=1 , the current candidate set (blue) is partitioned into K 1 = 4 K_{1}=4 contiguous chunks (dotted connectors). Using the level-1 key table ξ ( 1 ) \( \xi^{(1)} \) and message m ( 1 ) m^{(1)} , the sampler draws a chunk (solid arrows) and restricts the candidate set to the selected chunk (green). After the routing stage, the final token (black) is sampled from the remaining candidates using key table ξ ( 2 ) \( \xi^{(2)} \) and message m ( 2 ) m^{(2)} .

top_papers.title: SovereignPA-Bench: Evaluating User-Owned Personal Agents under Evolving Intent, Platform Mediation, and Consent Constraints
top_papers.abstract: SovereignPA-Bench introduces a novel benchmark to evaluate user-owned personal agents, focusing on their ability to uphold user sovereignty. It assesses agents across evolving user intent, platform mediation, and crucial constraints like privacy, consent, and resistance to manipulation, going beyond existing benchmarks that often overlook these aspects. The benchmark provides detailed component metrics to comprehensively measure an agent's performance in these critical areas.

top_papers.title: TREK: Distill to Explore, Reinforce to Refine
top_papers.abstract: TREK addresses the limitation of policy optimization methods that struggle with complex prompts by using distillation for exploration rather than imitation. It achieves this by identifying difficult prompts, obtaining verified solutions from a teacher, and then using these solutions to expand the student policy's exploration capabilities through a forward KL divergence phase. This staged approach allows TREK to efficiently improve performance on challenging tasks by strategically reinforcing promising solution modes.
top_papers.figure_caption: Summary of main results. (a)–(b): Math reasoning accuracy (avg@16, %) across Qwen3 scales on AIME 2025 and AIME 2024. TREK consistently improves over direct GRPO at all model sizes, with the DeepSeek-V4 proposal source outperforming the self-context variant. (c): ALFWorld success rate with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, showing analogous gains in the agentic planning domain. ScienceWorld results are reported in Table 2 .

top_papers.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark designed to evaluate vision-language models' ability to understand safety-critical incidents in dashcam videos. The core method involves a dataset of structured questions about real-world driving events, assessing models on their reasoning about contextual scene properties and incident details. The contribution is a standardized way to benchmark these models for reliable incident understanding in autonomous driving.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the VQA-Autopilot dataset annotation schema. The visualization illustrates the hierarchical structure of annotation categories, including environmental conditions, traffic context, incident types, outcomes, and associated attributes. This figure provides a high-level conceptual summary of the dataset design.

top_papers.title: Multi-Modal, Multi-Environment Machine Teaching for Robust Reward Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel machine teaching framework for robust reward learning in Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL). It addresses the limitation of existing methods by considering how diverse feedback modalities and multiple environments jointly influence reward function generalization. The core contribution is an analysis showing that different feedback types, particularly comparisons, offer stronger global constraints on rewards, leading to more robust and transferable objectives across varying operational contexts.

top_papers.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a proactive memory agent that actively intervenes in long-horizon tasks by injecting relevant memories when needed, rather than passively retrieving them. This agent updates a structured memory bank and decides whether to provide a reminder to an unmodified action agent. The core contribution is a plug-and-play module that significantly improves task completion rates by combating "behavioral state decay" in long trajectories.

top_papers.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
top_papers.abstract: This paper highlights that real patient communication with health chatbots is highly variable in content, emotion, and style, unlike typical simulated patients. The authors developed a novel patient simulator that captures these complexities and demonstrated its realism in a Turing-like test. Their contribution lies in showing how this communication diversity significantly impacts chatbot performance in urgency assessment, emphasizing the need for patient-centered AI that accounts for these variations.

top_papers.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
top_papers.abstract: UltraX introduces a novel programmatic editing framework for large-scale pre-training data, addressing limitations of existing methods. Its core contribution is a function-calling approach that enables fine-grained instance-level editing through insertion, deletion, and modification, powered by a reliable program-supervision generation pipeline. This allows for more efficient and effective refinement of LLM training data as scaling laws plateau.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overall workflow of UltraX, covering program-supervision generation, refinement model training, and inference-time program execution.

top_papers.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual model for LLM workflows, representing them as persistent knowledge objects. The core method involves distinguishing between deterministic "derive" operations and LLM-mediated "infer" judgments, all managed within a shared knowledge substrate. This approach enables semantic persistence, allowing workflows themselves to be treated as knowledge, not just producers of it.
top_papers.figure_caption: Semantic workflow objects are interpreted by the DSL-machine control layer, which coordinates runtime services and writes back workflow instances, mediated effects, and records of inference, approval, and panel activity. The bidirectional relation indicates that the control layer both reads semantic objects and writes back persistent semantic objects or relations.

top_papers.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
top_papers.abstract: UniClawBench is a novel benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents in real-world scenarios. Its core method involves assessing agents based on five foundational capabilities: skill usage, exploration, long-context reasoning, multimodal understanding, and cross-platform coordination. The contribution lies in providing a capability-driven framework with 400 bilingual tasks, enabling more precise identification of agent weaknesses beyond traditional sandboxed, single-turn evaluations.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of UniClawBench. UniClawBench consists of 400 bilingual real-world tasks spanning 5 core capabilities: multimodal, long-context, skill usage, exploration, and cross-platform. We propose a three-role closed-loop evaluation framework, where an executor agent performs tasks in real environments, a supervisor evaluates trajectories and artifacts using hidden rubrics, and a user simulator provides natural feedback based on executor’s performance and supervisor’s signal, enabling multi-turn interaction. We conduct two sets of experiments to evaluate cross-model and cross-framework performance. The capability-level results reveal that framework choice exerts a stronger influence than model choice.

top_papers.title: All Explanations are Wrong, But Many Are Useful: Exploring the Rashomon Explanation Set with Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper challenges the accuracy-explainability trade-off in AI by proposing the "Rashomon Explanation" paradigm. Instead of a single explanation, it generates a set of faithful, prediction-guiding explanations. The proposed RashomonLLM workflow uses Large Language Models to iteratively align explanations with predictions, improving both accuracy and explainability.

top_papers.title: Decoupling Language Guidance from Backbones for Text-Guided Medical Segmentation
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes BTHA, a framework that decouples language guidance from medical image segmentation backbones. Its core method uses shape-preserving adapters to inject semantic guidance at a stable feature level, allowing for reuse across different vision and text models. The main contribution is enabling backbone transferability and a more flexible approach to text-guided segmentation through a hierarchical coarse-to-fine supervision strategy.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison between existing text-guided segmentation paradigms and our proposed method. Existing methods require fusion redesigns when backbones change, leading to limited reuse. Conversely, our method introduces a shape-preserving interface, enabling module reuse across diverse backbones.

top_papers.title: ProofCouncil: An LLM Agent for Solving Open Mathematical Problems
top_papers.abstract: ProofCouncil is an LLM agent designed to solve open mathematical problems by mimicking real-world mathematical practice through an author-critic architecture. Its core method involves an iterative process where an "author" generates potential solutions and a "critic" evaluates and refines them. The paper's main contribution is demonstrating ProofCouncil's strong performance on challenging open problems, outperforming other agents in the FirstProof challenge and showing significant promise on a dataset of researcher-sourced problems.

top_papers.title: SAGEAgent: A Self-Evolving Agent for Cost-Aware Modality Acquisition in Multimodal Survival Prediction
top_papers.abstract: SAGEAgent addresses the challenge of cost-effectively acquiring diagnostic modalities for cancer survival prediction. It acts as a self-evolving LLM-based agent that intelligently decides which tests to perform for each patient, balancing improved prediction accuracy against the invasiveness and cost of further diagnostics. This novel approach frames modality acquisition as a sequential decision problem, optimizing resource allocation in clinical oncology.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of modality acquisition strategies. (a) Existing approaches: static fusion applies all modalities uniformly, RL learns adaptive policies without explanation, and LLM-based methods reason over independent tests without clinical ordering. (b) SAGEAgent follows a clinically acquisition order, deciding at each stage whether to acquire or stop based on clinical tools, learned rules, and similar past cases. Patient A stops early (83% burden saved); Patient B proceeds through all modalities.

top_papers.title: Scalable Visual Pretraining for Language Intelligence
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to pretraining language models by directly incorporating visual information from documents, rather than relying solely on extracted text. Their core method involves unsupervised visual pretraining on raw visual documents, demonstrating that this "visual pretraining" is a scalable learner. The key contribution is showing that this visual approach consistently outperforms text-only pretraining for enhancing language intelligence across various benchmarks.

top_papers.title: Task-Specific Multimodal Question Answering Agents via Confidence Calibration and Incremental Reasoning for QANTA 2026
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a task-specific, two-agent architecture for multimodal question answering in the QANTA 2026 challenge. The core method involves a "Tossup" agent using a smaller GPT model with confidence calibration and numeric reasoning to handle uncertainty, and a "Bonus" agent employing a larger GPT model with lead-in awareness for accurate answer selection. Their contribution is a novel approach to adapt multimodal QA agents to distinct task objectives, improving performance under efficiency constraints.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the proposed QANTA 2026 system. The Tossup agent combines evidence routing, confidence calibration, a Numeric Firewall, and expected-value-based buzzing, while the Bonus agent performs leadin-aware multimodal reasoning and evidence fusion.

top_papers.title: TrustX Agent Risk Classification Framework (ARC): Risk-Tiering Internally Created Agentic AI Systems
top_papers.abstract: The TrustX Agent Risk Classification Framework (ARC) addresses the growing need for specialized AI governance by introducing a structured method to classify agentic AI systems. Its core is a twelve-dimension scoring rubric, combined with classification models and an autonomy framework, to quantify risk and generate tiered governance recommendations with mapped controls. This framework's contribution lies in providing a repeatable, robust instrument for governing the unique risks posed by internally created agentic AI systems.

top_papers.title: Agent Hacks Agent: Autoresearch for Production-Agent Red-Teaming
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AHA, an automated red-teaming method for LLM agents. It uses one agent to discover vulnerabilities in another by proposing hypotheses, constructing falsifiers, and executing attacks in a sandbox. AHA's contribution is a "Vulnerability Concept Graph" that captures reusable knowledge about enabling conditions for unsafe agent behavior, moving beyond simply recording attack successes.
top_papers.figure_caption: AHA overview. An autoresearch loop turns executed red-team trajectories into a frozen, reusable VCG, the auditable artifact this paper produces and evaluates.

top_papers.title: An Explainable Agentic System for Detection of Conversational Scams with Summary-Based Memory
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces an explainable agentic system to detect sophisticated, multi-turn conversational scams, addressing the limitations of single-message detectors. The system utilizes a summary-based memory to track scam progression and provides explanations for its detections. A key contribution is ConScamBench-278, a new benchmark dataset for conversational scam detection, enabling reproducible research and evaluation.
top_papers.figure_caption: The URL extraction and analysis pipeline. The system replaces third-party API dependencies with a local headless browser and Docling to prevent data leakage and tracking while improving the analysis of dynamic, JavaScript-heavy phishing content.

top_papers.title: From World Action Models to Embodied Brains: A Roadmap for Open-World Physical Intelligence
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that achieving artificial general intelligence in the physical world requires integrating existing approaches like action models and world models into a unified framework. The authors identify key fragmentation issues in current research and propose a roadmap centered on the "embodied brain" concept. This embodied brain would act as a central component for multimodal reasoning, intervention comparison, and issuing action commands, fostering a more cohesive and progressive research direction.
top_papers.figure_caption: System-level progression from WAM research to an embodied brain and a co-evolving physical-intelligence stack. WAMs provide a current route for studying intervention-conditioned prediction, while the embodied brain remains the broader target for reusable physical reasoning and intent formation.

top_papers.title: MM-ToolSandBox: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Visual Tool-Calling Agents
top_papers.abstract: MM-ToolSandBox is a unified framework for evaluating visual tool-calling agents. It provides a stateful execution environment with over 500 tools across 16 domains, supporting complex multi-turn, multi-image tasks. The framework's contribution lies in its realistic simulation of conversational phenomena and its automated scenario generation, revealing that current state-of-the-art models struggle with robust visual tool-calling, achieving less than 50% success.

top_papers.title: When Local Monitors Miss Compositional Harm: Diagnosing Distributed Backdoors in Multi-Agent Systems
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "distributed backdoors" in multi-agent LLM systems, where a harmful payload is split across agents, making each individual step appear benign to local monitors. The core contribution is demonstrating that traditional local monitoring is insufficient because these distributed attacks exploit an "observability boundary," where the fragmented harm becomes indistinguishable from normal traffic. The paper proves that once fragments appear locally benign, no monitor operating solely on that local view can detect the attack.

top_papers.title: How Temperature Shapes Ideological Discourse in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how ideological biases in retrieved information affect LLM outputs within Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The researchers used Lexical Multidimensional Analysis to identify ideological discourses in COVID-19 treatment articles, then employed these as a knowledge source for RAG. By varying sampling temperatures, they demonstrated that RAG can transmit, amplify, or suppress these ideological viewpoints in LLM-generated answers.
top_papers.figure_caption: Factor scores.

top_papers.title: Production and Perception in LLMs: A Token Probability Approach
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit a production-perception asymmetry similar to humans. The core method involves comparing token probabilities generated by an LLM under "production" prompts (e.g., generating a poem) versus "perception" prompts (e.g., re-scoring existing tokens). The key contribution is demonstrating a consistent and significant difference in token probabilities between production and perception tasks, suggesting LLMs may functionally mirror this psycholinguistic distinction.

top_papers.title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques
top_papers.abstract: This survey introduces a unified framework to analyze and accelerate the inference of masked diffusion large language models (dLLMs). It categorizes existing techniques across algorithms, architectures, and systems, aiming to disentangle their impact on end-to-end latency and guide future research towards practical speedups. The core contribution is a structured approach to understanding and improving dLLM inference efficiency, moving beyond simple parallel generation.

top_papers.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces E3 (Estimate, Execute, Expand), a method for AI agents to assess task complexity before execution. E3 estimates the necessary scope, executes a minimal path, and only expands if verification fails. This approach significantly reduces computational cost and resource usage while maintaining high success rates.
top_papers.figure_caption: The E3 framework. The agent estimates an initial operating point x 0 = ( d ^ , s ^ , r ^ , c ^ ) x_{0}=(\( \hat{d} \),\( \hat{s} \),\( \hat{r} \),\( \hat{c} \)) , executes a minimum viable path sized to x 0 x_{0} , and expands scope only when verification fails or confidence is low. Successful verification exits immediately.

top_papers.title: FormalAnalyticGeo: A Neural-Symbolic Based Framework for Multimodal Analytic Geometry Problem Generation
top_papers.abstract: FormalAnalyticGeo addresses the lack of annotated data in multimodal analytic geometry by introducing a novel neural-symbolic framework. Its core method uses a formal intermediate representation (CDL) to bridge natural language problem descriptions with precise diagram generation via an SDF engine. This allows for the scalable, automatic creation of diverse and geometrically accurate analytic geometry problems.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Diagram generation for the same analytic geometry problem. (a) ChatGPT: the circle does not use the focal distance as its diameter, and P P lies on the circle but not on the hyperbola. (b) Nano Banana: geometrically meaningless output. (c) Gemini 3 Pro: distorted curves and inaccurate point placement. (d) Ours: geometrically exact rendering with known coordinate-to-pixel mapping, enabling direct visual measurement of ground-truth answers.

top_papers.title: Human-AI Agent Interaction as a Neuroplastic Training Environment
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes that everyday human-AI agent interactions, characterized by an iterative request-response-appraisal loop, act as an unrecognized neuroplastic training environment. The authors argue that repeated exposure to disappointing AI outputs can inadvertently strengthen negative cognitive patterns like impatience and frustration. Their core contribution is the idea that this same environment can be intentionally leveraged to cultivate positive neuroplastic changes and desirable cognitive habits.
top_papers.figure_caption: What an AI agent is, and why its use forms a loop. A person issues a request in natural language; the agent — an AI system built on a large language or generative model — returns a result, which the person then evaluates. Because the result rarely matches the intention on the first attempt, the person reacts and issues a revised request, and the exchange repeats. However different such tools appear — conversational assistants, coding copilots, image or text generators — their use shares one shape: an iterative loop of request, result, reaction, and revision. The reaction phase (highlighted) is the moment this paper concerns.

top_papers.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MemOps, a new benchmark for evaluating long-term memory in LLM agents. Instead of just checking final answers, MemOps analyzes the sequence of memory operations (remembering, forgetting, updating, etc.) throughout a conversation. This allows for a more granular assessment of memory performance, identifying specific failure points beyond just incorrect outputs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison between existing long-term memory benchmark and our MemOps .

top_papers.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
top_papers.abstract: PalmClaw is a novel on-device agent framework for mobile phones. Its core method involves running LLM agents natively on the device, enabling direct access to mobile capabilities as structured tools. This contribution allows for more efficient and integrated task automation on smartphones, overcoming limitations of existing GUI-based approaches.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of PalmClaw. (a) An externally hosted mobile agent exchanges GUI states and GUI actions between a desktop or cloud host and the phone. (b) PalmClaw runs the agent components on the mobile device and connects them to device resources and capabilities through device tools.

top_papers.title: Who Grades the Grader? Co-Evolving Evaluation Metrics and Skills for Self-Improving LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces **Double Ratchet**, a method for co-evolving evaluation metrics and agent skills in a self-improving LLM system. Instead of assuming a pre-existing metric, it dynamically creates and refines metrics by composing smaller detectors, trained to align with human-defined anchors and consensus. This approach allows LLM agents to improve their performance on tasks where reliable evaluation metrics are initially absent, demonstrating significant gains across various benchmarks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Double Ratchet architecture. The metric loop (left) evolves an expression over drawback detectors; the skill loop (right) evolves the agent’s skill bank, its training graded by the evolved metric during co-evolution. Anchors (bottom) are never trained on; an independent judge audits final outputs on reference-free tasks.

top_papers.title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the reliability of LLM-generated rubrics for evaluating open-ended outputs in research paper reproduction. The core method involves a meta-evaluation of LLM-generated rubrics, reformulated as checklists, assessing their semantic similarity and alignment with human-generated rubrics. The key contribution is demonstrating that augmented LLM rubric generation significantly improves downstream evaluation alignment, approaching human performance, thus offering a more scalable solution for benchmark creation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our meta-evaluation framework for LLM-generated rubrics in paper reproduction. Given a paper, reproduction agents generate candidate repositories, while LLMs and human experts produce checklist-style rubrics. We evaluate generated rubrics intrinsically by measuring their semantic similarity to human-authored rubrics, and extrinsically by comparing the repository scores they induce with PaperBench evaluations.

top_papers.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Knowledge-Less Language Models (KLLMs), a new training method that anonymizes named entities during pretraining. This approach suppresses reliance on memorized factual knowledge, shifting models towards reasoning based on provided context. KLLMs demonstrate improved performance on tasks requiring evidence-grounded reasoning, such as contextual question answering and fact verification, while reducing factual recall.
top_papers.figure_caption: Pipeline of Knowledgeless Language Model (KLLM) training and inference

top_papers.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context
top_papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that while LLMs appear robust to task-irrelevant context at an aggregate accuracy level, this stability masks significant per-example prediction flips. Even semantically meaningless context can alter predictions for a subset of inputs, revealing a hidden fragility in LLM behavior that is model-specific and influenced by various factors.
top_papers.figure_caption: Context-induced instability is a two-sided effect. We show two MMLU-Pro examples where task-irrelevant context respectively improves and degrades gpt-5.4 ’s responses by affecting commonsense and calculation. Full examples are in Appendix I .

top_papers.title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces HealthClaw, a novel agent architecture for longitudinal personal health management. Its core method involves a self-evolving mechanism that continuously updates its understanding of a user's changing health profile, preferences, and risks over time. HealthClaw's key contribution is its ability to significantly improve answer accuracy and reduce context exposure compared to traditional methods, while also enhancing privacy-aware responses.
top_papers.figure_caption: Unified architecture of HealthClaw: closed-loop interaction and five-layer evolving memory. The top row shows the closed interaction loop. A, Perception integrates three input streams (wearables and devices, prior records and ongoing dialogue) into a current health context. B, Reasoning performs memory-informed task planning through knowledge retrieval, sub-problem decomposition and constrained plan formulation. C, Action executes the plan iteratively through tool invocation, intermediate-result checking and plan refinement, producing user-facing outputs. D, Induction operates after each episode to determine what should be carried forward by consolidating user facts, revising reusable task procedures and preserving episode traces. The bottom panel, E, shows the five-layer evolving memory. L0 (behavioural rules) and L1 (domain knowledge index) are shared domain-level layers, whereas L2 (privacy-critical personal profile), L3 (reusable task standard operating procedures, SOPs) and L4 (episodic memory) are personalized user-level layers. In this design, L2 stores sensitive profile information locally rather than exposing raw identifiable memory payloads during retrieval. Memory read supports planning in B, and memory writeback from D updates the user-level layers after each completed episode, enabling longitudinal personalization through incremental accumulation rather than one-shot responses.

top_papers.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Deep Interaction," an efficient method for correcting reasoning errors in large language models. Instead of simply re-generating, it allows users to directly edit faulty steps within the model's reasoning chain. This edited chain is then distilled into a prompt, guiding the LLM to follow the corrected path, significantly improving correction success and reducing token usage.
top_papers.figure_caption: A simple case shows the different pipeline between dialogue-based method and Deep Interaction. Dialogue-based feedback may leave the model on an incorrect reasoning trajectory, while Deep Interaction enables more fine-grained editing of the CoT.

top_papers.title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Experience Memory Graph (EMG) to address error recovery in LLM agents. EMG reformulates failure correction as a graph matching problem, converting failed and successful trajectories into directed action decision graphs. By matching these graphs, it identifies successful workflows and explicit correction paths, enabling one-shot error recovery without costly iterative reflection.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Difference of error correction based on (a) reflect-replay loop and (b) Experience Memory Graph. Existing methods rely on iterative test‑time reflection — the agent replans and re‑executes after each failure, causing high latency and cost. Our Experience Memory Graph extracts error correction paths offline by computing graph edit paths that transform failed trajectories into successful ones from paired training trajectories of the same task, distills them into insights, and stores them in a memory graph. At test time, retrieval enables one‑shot exectution without loops.

top_papers.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation
top_papers.abstract: This paper redefines penetration testing for AI-enabled systems, shifting the focus from traditional resource compromise to the violation of behavioral objectives. The core method involves inducing AI-governed behavior that deviates from intended operational outcomes, rather than solely exploiting infrastructure vulnerabilities. This contribution extends security evaluation to address the unique attack surface of AI systems, where influencing learned models can lead to undesirable behaviors.

top_papers.title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the DVM-HALL model to address how autonomous AI agents impact customer loyalty. It proposes a framework where human emotions, agent utility, trust, and verifiable execution jointly determine brand choice, moving beyond traditional loyalty concepts. The core contribution is a dynamic, multi-agent model that accounts for AI's evolving capabilities in autonomous commerce.
top_papers.figure_caption: The Tripartite DVM-HALL Architecture, illustrating the bidirectional flows of trust, algorithmic loyalty, and emotional brand equity governed by overarching oversight frameworks across a multi-agent marketplace (human, personal agent, seller agents, and payment/settlement agents).

top_papers.title: Unleashing Multimodal Large Language Models for Training-free HOI Detection in the Wild
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AgentHOI, a novel training-free framework for human-object interaction (HOI) detection. It leverages the inherent multimodal reasoning capabilities of foundation models, moving beyond simple prompting to enable more robust and generalizable HOI detection in open-world scenarios. The core contribution lies in its agentic approach, allowing for contextual reasoning without requiring dataset-specific supervision.
top_papers.figure_caption: Framework comparison with previous methods. Most existing methods depend on manually annotated, large-scale HOI datasets for training, which is both time-consuming and resource-intensive. Moreover, they often exhibit limited generalizability in real-world settings. In contrast, our AgentHOI framework requires no annotation or training, offering strong generalizability by leveraging off-the-shelf vision foundation models.

top_papers.title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
top_papers.abstract: TRACE addresses the challenge of assigning credit in long-horizon multi-turn agents by estimating rewards at each tool-call turn. It leverages a frozen reference model to calculate log-probabilities of the correct answer, transforming these into state values. By computing Temporal-Difference changes in these values, TRACE derives dense, per-action rewards, overcoming the sparsity and high variance of outcome-only rewards.
top_papers.figure_caption: Credit assignment at tool-call boundaries in a search trajectory. The figure illustrates a long-horizon search rollout decomposed into tool-call turns. Early search and open actions can add task-relevant evidence to the transcript even when a later branch leads to an incorrect final answer. Outcome-reward training attaches one trajectory-level advantage to all actions in the rollout, whereas TRACE computes prefix values at tool boundaries and assigns turn credit from adjacent value changes.

top_papers.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
top_papers.abstract: DeepStress is a novel framework for stress-testing deep search agents by replacing their retrieval module with a controlled synthetic environment. This allows for systematic manipulation of evidence quality across trustworthiness, relevance, and factuality. The paper's contribution lies in demonstrating significant performance disparities among agents when faced with unreliable information and proposing new metrics to better evaluate their robustness and knowledge interaction.

top_papers.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
top_papers.abstract: AutoSynthesis is an end-to-end multi-agent system that automates the entire meta-analysis process, from formulating search strategies to generating PRISMA-compliant reports. Its core method involves a series of agents that handle literature retrieval, screening, data extraction, and statistical analysis. The main contribution is enabling scalable and efficient quantitative evidence synthesis, significantly reducing the manual effort typically required.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the AutoSynthesis framework. A multi-agent framework including: a , The workflow begins by transforming the user’s research question into a structured review protocol and retrieving candidate studies from multiple scientific databases using LLM-generated search queries. b , Retrieved articles undergo full-text retrieval, eligibility assessment, and study mapping, where independent studies and research questions are identified within each paper. c , Statistical evidence is extracted, validated against the source article, and filtered to retain only the results relevant to the target meta-analysis before being standardized into a common representation. d , Standardized effect sizes are synthesized using a random-effects meta-analysis, followed by publication-bias assessment and automatic generation of a PRISMA-compliant report together with visualizations and complete audit records. The modular architecture enables every stage of the evidence-synthesis process to be independently inspected, verified, and compared with expert-conducted meta-analysis.

top_papers.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Scientific Visualization Literacy
top_papers.abstract: This paper benchmarks six multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on a scientific visualization literacy assessment. The core method involves evaluating MLLMs against human performance on a standardized test covering various visualization techniques and tasks. The key contribution is demonstrating that current MLLMs have uneven scientific visualization literacy, with Gemini showing promising results while open-source models lag behind human capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: \( \hot \) Model and human performance across different techniques in SVLAT. Each dot shows the mean accuracy, with the bars indicating 95% confidence intervals.

top_papers.title: BrainPilot: Automating Brain Discovery with Agentic Research
top_papers.abstract: BrainPilot is a fully open-source multi-agent system designed to automate brain science research. Its core method involves a principal investigator (PI) agent coordinating specialist agents, all grounded in curated domain knowledge, to perform complex research tasks. The system's main contribution is accelerating discovery by providing traceable logs and agent-verified results, addressing limitations of current AI agents in domain expertise and reliability for brain science.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of BrainPilot. (a) A curated knowledge base and skill library, built from neuroscience textbooks and papers, feed a harness in which a principal investigator (PI) agent coordinates specialist agents. (b) The targeted breadth of brain science research, from systems and circuits to cognition, disease, and foundational machine learning. (c) The researcher interacts with the PI agent, which delegates tasks to specialist agents while keeping the researcher in the loop.

top_papers.title: Digital Pantheon: Simulating and Auditing Coalition Formation with LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Digital Pantheon," a novel multi-agent framework for simulating political coalition formation. It combines SFT, DPO, and RAG to enable LLM agents to exhibit both factual grounding and strong partisan behavior, overcoming RLHF limitations. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to create realistic, ideologically aligned agents for simulating complex negotiations and its introduction of a "Multi-Layered Information Lineage Topology" for interpreting these emergent dynamics.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the individual party alignment model process.

top_papers.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning method for Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) by addressing the intractability of log-likelihood estimation. The core method formalizes DLM generation as a two-stage action Markov Decision Process, decomposing the policy gradient into token and masking terms. This dual optimization significantly improves performance on reasoning and coding tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmarks like GSM8K and MBPP.
top_papers.figure_caption: Test accuracy of our method and baseline methods on two mathematical reasoning and two code generation benchmarks. All methods use LLaDA-8B-Instruct as the base model and are evaluated with a generation length of 128. Full results are provided in Table 1 .

top_papers.title: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
top_papers.abstract: Plover addresses the challenge of GUI automation by externalizing task plans, making them inspectable and editable. This "plan-centric" approach allows users to supervise, correct, and guide the agent's actions directly on the plan, preserving progress during repairs. The core contribution is enabling explicit user control and adaptation in dynamic GUI environments.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. The Plover system architecture.

top_papers.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
top_papers.abstract: RoboTTT scales robot policy context to 8,000 timesteps by using Test-Time Training (TTT) to update model parameters (fast weights) during inference. This allows robot foundation models to process long histories without increased latency, enabling capabilities like one-shot imitation, on-the-fly policy improvement, and better performance on long-horizon tasks. The core contribution is demonstrating that significantly longer context, achieved through TTT, unlocks new robot abilities and improves performance.

top_papers.title: Scaling Behavior Foundation Model for Humanoid Robots
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a coordinated scaling approach for Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) in humanoid robot control. Their core method reformulates diverse control problems as motion tracking, enabling the reproduction of integrated whole-body movements. This coordinated scaling of learning paradigm, data, and architecture leads to significant performance improvements and enhanced generalization for humanoid robots.

top_papers.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
top_papers.abstract: SceneBind creates an omni-modal representation that jointly understands the "what" and "where" of realistic scenes across vision, audio, and language. Its core method uses object-centric semantic-spatial slots to explicitly capture object semantics, spatial attributes, and uncertainty, addressing the lack of spatial structure in existing omni-modal models. This representation enables cross-modal scene retrieval and object grounding through a novel semantic-spatial matching scheme.
top_papers.figure_caption: SceneBind models scenes by jointly capturing semantics ( what ) and 3D spatial attributes ( where ) across vision, audio and language. SceneBind maps each modality into a shared global embedding with object-centric slots, enabling semantic–spatial representation of multimodal scenes.

top_papers.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SearchOS-V1, a multi-agent framework designed to improve open-domain information-seeking agents. Its core method involves explicitly tracking task progress by representing information seeking as relational schema completion with grounded citations. The key contribution is the Search-Oriented Context Management (SOCM) system, which externalizes and shares the evolving state through components like a Frontier Task, Evidence Graph, Coverage Map, and Failure Memory, preventing agents from getting stuck in repetitive search loops.
top_papers.figure_caption: SearchOS interface for a long-horizon information-seeking task. The workspace exposes the orchestration trace, pipeline parallel agent activity, and relational schema coverage.

top_papers.title: AlphaWiSE: Adaptive Weight Interpolation for Continual Multimodal Representation Learning
top_papers.abstract: AlphaWiSE addresses the challenge of maintaining cross-modal alignment in continual multimodal learning by proposing a post-hoc weight interpolation method. It composes two frozen checkpoints by fitting a single scalar coefficient per parameter tensor, allowing for adaptive weight blending. This approach creates a single interpolated checkpoint that balances stability and plasticity without increasing inference time, leading to improved cross-modal retrieval performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: AlphaWiSE performs post-hoc, per-tensor fusion of two compatible continual-learning checkpoints. Both source checkpoints remain frozen. The exemplar memory is used only to optimize the coefficients 𝜷 \( \bm{\beta} \) , with α p = σ ​ ( β p ) \( \alpha_{p} \)=\( \sigma \)(\( \beta_{p} \)) and θ ~ p = α p ​ θ p un + ( 1 − α p ) ​ θ p reg \( \tilde{\theta}_{p} \)=\( \alpha_{p} \)\( \theta_{p} \)^{\( \mathrm{un} \)}+(1-\( \alpha_{p} \))\( \theta_{p} \)^{\( \mathrm{reg} \)} . After optimization, the fused tensors are materialized into one checkpoint. The final model has the same architecture and inference-time computation as either source checkpoint.

top_papers.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces BadWAM, a framework for evaluating adversarial attacks on World-Action Models (WAMs). It demonstrates that small visual perturbations can break the crucial link between a WAM's predicted future and its actual executed actions. BadWAM highlights that WAMs, despite their promise, are vulnerable to these "World-Action Drift Attacks," which can be tuned for either maximum disruption or stealth.
top_papers.figure_caption: Empirical motivation for world-action adversarial attacks. Failed episodes tend to have larger action shifts, while predicted-future shifts overlap across successful and failed executions. This motivates attacking the alignment between action and imagination.

top_papers.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that traditional methods of evaluating retrieval systems, which assess a document's usefulness in isolation, fail to capture its true value in multi-step agentic search. The authors introduce Counterfactual Trajectory Utility (CTU) to measure how a document's presence impacts an agent's subsequent actions and overall success. Their findings demonstrate a significant disconnect between static retrieval utility and this dynamic, causal utility.

top_papers.title: Rubrics on Trial: Evolving Rubrics from a Single Query via Synthetic Pairwise Evidence
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Rubrics on Trial," a novel method for automatically generating and refining rubrics for LLMs using only a single query. It synthesizes pairwise response evidence conditioned on candidate rubrics, validating each rubric's ability to discriminate answer quality before inclusion. This approach avoids external annotations and model training, effectively screening out unhelpful rubrics and improving LLM evaluation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of Rubrics on Trial . At evolution step t t , a proposer suggests an Add or Split patch. Response generators construct two rubric-conditioned pairs for each candidate rubric under the same trial background ℬ t \( \mathcal{B}_{t} \) . A rubric-blind judge independently compares each pair in both orders. A deterministic lookup decides whether the patch updates the active-leaf rubric set, while both accepted and rejected outcomes enter evolution memory.

top_papers.title: An Exam for Active Observers
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ActiveVision, a new benchmark designed to evaluate whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) engage in active observation, mirroring human vision's continuous gaze redirection. The benchmark's tasks require repeated visual perception, unlike static image descriptions. Frontier MLLMs perform poorly on ActiveVision, solving a mere fraction of tasks compared to human participants, highlighting a significant gap in their visual reasoning capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Seeing is not always a single-glance task. Many visual problems require an observer to coordinate attention and memory across an image: scanning exhaustively for distributed evidence, following connected structures without losing track, and comparing fine-grained attributes across distant regions. ActiveVision turns these abilities into a controlled test of whether MLLMs can keep visual evidence in the reasoning loop.

top_papers.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
top_papers.abstract: This paper evaluates open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) for automatically generating structured threat information (STIX) from plain-text descriptions of vulnerabilities in Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs). The core contribution is the creation of the CAV-STIXGen dataset and the demonstration of LLMs' capability to extract and format complex security data, aiding practitioners in better understanding and mitigating CAV risks.
top_papers.figure_caption: An Example of CVE Description to STIX Generation.

top_papers.title: Frontier AI performance across the business disciplines: a case-grounded benchmark of knowledge work and analytical reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces BusinessCaseBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Frontier AI performance on complex analytical knowledge work, a domain poorly captured by existing AI tests. The benchmark leverages the case method from business education, presenting AI with real-world scenarios requiring synthesis, judgment under uncertainty, strategic thinking, and structured analysis. Its contribution lies in providing a more realistic assessment of AI's capabilities for white-collar professionals.
top_papers.figure_caption: The evaluation pipeline used to construct and score BusinessCaseBench. Case narratives and open-ended questions are paired with expert-written reference solutions from the instructor case solution. The reference solutions are transformed into equally-weighted checklist rubrics. A frontier AI model receives the case and question, produces an attempted solution, and an LLM-as-judge model scores the solution against each rubric criterion compared to the reference solution. Scores aggregate to Standard scoring (partial credit) and Complete Answer scoring (all criteria satisfied) metrics reported throughout the paper. We use human annotators to validate the automatic grading.

top_papers.title: SciForge: An AI-Native, Multimodal Workbench for Scientific Discovery
top_papers.abstract: SciForge is an AI-native workbench designed for scientific discovery by treating diverse research artifacts as coherent, auditable entities. Its core method involves a "translate-then-reason" approach for multimodal inputs, where scientific objects are first translated before AI agents process them. The key contribution is enabling goal-oriented, auditable research through structured decision governance and evidence traceability, while keeping the graphical interface for human oversight.
top_papers.figure_caption: SciForge at a glance: a live scientific-research thread (left) and its inspectable Evidence DAG (right). In this target-discovery example, source assertions, reasoning nodes, and claims remain connected to support and contradiction edges, while node-level provenance and audit metrics stay visible to the researcher.

top_papers.title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
top_papers.abstract: This paper analyzes multi-agent systems (MAS) versus single-agent systems (SAS) using an information bottleneck framework. It highlights that MAS's advantage over SAS emerges under bounded communication, where agents must compress information. This compression creates a trade-off between efficiency and information loss, which the paper formalizes as an information bottleneck controlled by a parameter $\beta$.
top_papers.figure_caption: Predicted MAS gain by relay regime. MAS helps when context reduction outweighs capability-weighted relay loss; stronger models gain less from compression and lose more from information loss.

top_papers.title: DELUGE: Towards Continental-Scale Daily Pluvial Flood Damage Prediction via Interpretable Conditioning on Foundation Model Embeddings
top_papers.abstract: DELUGE is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts daily pluvial flood damage at a ~1 km resolution across the continental US. It achieves this by conditioning a foundation model on interpretable hazard, exposure, and vulnerability components, focusing on high-claim regions to improve efficiency and accuracy. The core contribution is enabling continental-scale, daily pluvial flood damage prediction, overcoming limitations of previous coarse-resolution or computationally intensive methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Our study region in blue. We select the Top 100 75 × \( \times \) 75 km grid cells for NFIP pluvial flood damage claims, accounting for ∼ \( \sim \) 81% of claims from 2017–2022. After rasterizing NFIP claims (see § 3.1.1 ,§ 3.1.2 ), training samples take the form of ( pixel , day) tuples, and DELUGE takes input a ∼ \( \sim \) 8x8km patch centered around the pixel as spatial context.

top_papers.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization
top_papers.abstract: PagedWeight addresses the memory bottleneck in serving Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs by dynamically quantizing expert weights at runtime. This method intelligently balances model accuracy with KV cache size, leading to significant GPU memory savings and improved throughput. Its core contribution is a novel quality-aware quantization strategy that optimizes the trade-off between performance and memory consumption for MoE LLM serving.
top_papers.figure_caption: Static quantization fixes MoE weights; PagedWeight offloads weight pages to free KV cache headroom.

top_papers.title: BayesPO: Bayesian Prompt Optimization via Parallel-Tempered Gradient-Guided Discrete MCMC
top_papers.abstract: This paper frames prompt optimization as Bayesian posterior sampling, combining a task-specific likelihood with a language model prior to favor effective and fluent prompts. It then uses gradient-guided discrete Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with parallel tempering to efficiently explore the prompt space, offering a principled approach beyond heuristic search.

top_papers.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to compare different text encodings (tokens, bytes, pixels) by controlling both the linguistic content and the model's capacity. By sweeping a shared bottleneck, they generate rate-utility frontiers to isolate the number of input positions, latent capacity, and task-relevant information. Their contribution is a principled comparison revealing that no single encoding excels across all tasks and capacity levels, with pixels best for surface form and bytes for cross-lingual alignment.
top_papers.figure_caption: The same linguistic content produces different source rates across encodings and languages. Each column shows a translation of the same SIB-200 sentence, with token, byte, and pixel patch lengths annotated. A fixed input length does not expose equal content across representations to a model. For example, Chinese is longer than English in tokens, even with tokenizers re-trained on matched-content and regime specific languages, but shorter in bytes and patches. Our experiments examine how source rate differences interact with bottleneck capacity across tasks that require different kinds of information.

top_papers.title: Can We Break LLMs Out of Self-Loops? Fine-Grained Reasoning Control with Activation Steering
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SOPHIA, a method to control LLM reasoning by intervening on their internal latent states. It identifies that LLM reasoning failures often manifest as self-loops in these states. SOPHIA statistically characterizes these states and steers LLMs away from self-loops during inference, offering fine-grained control over the reasoning process beyond prompt-based methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: Self-loops in LRM reasoning traces. The model computes the correct value early (purple, $64) but cycles through redundant verification and re-questioning steps (red) before committing, wasting budget on work it has already done. Box colors denote latent reasoning states K = 5 K=5 that are induced unsupervisedly from activations rather than assigned from a hand-defined thought taxonomy Chen et al. ( 2025 ) , with transitions discovered automatically from generated traces. This makes failure modes like the loop above targetable as transition events at finer granularity than token- or prompt-level control allows.

top_papers.title: Do Language Models Dream of Binding Molecules? Benchmarking LLMs under Spatial Constraints
top_papers.abstract: This paper benchmarks general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) against specialized diffusion models for 3D molecule generation under spatial constraints relevant to drug design. The core method involves evaluating LLMs' ability to incorporate complex 3D information, such as anchor fragments and interaction points, into ligand generation. The contribution is a systematic analysis and a new benchmark (3D-Fit) to assess LLMs' spatial reasoning capabilities in this critical domain.

top_papers.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models for Whole-Slide and Tumor Microenvironment Analysis
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, efficient foundation models for whole-slide pathology and spatial proteomics. Their core method involves a distilled, compact tile encoder shared between models, enabling efficient learning of transferable representations from large-scale histopathology data. The main contribution is overcoming computational limitations of existing models, making large-scale slide-level analysis more accessible for clinical and research applications.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the GigaPath/GigaTIME model family. GigaPath-Flash provides efficient tile and slide encoders at 22M parameters. GigaTIME predicts spatial proteomics from H&E, scaling from CNN (9M) to ViT backbones.

top_papers.title: LLMs and Agentic AI Systems for Smart Grids: A Tutorial on Architectures and Applications
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a "solver-grounded" design principle for LLM-based agentic AI systems in smart grids, ensuring numerical outputs are from trusted tools and explicitly verified. This addresses the lack of unified design and evaluation methods, preventing physically infeasible results. The contribution lies in providing a principled framework and reviewing architectures and applications for this emerging domain.
top_papers.figure_caption: Solver-grounded LLM and agentic workflow for smart grids. (a) Conventional power system studies rely on trusted numerical tools, followed by explicit verification before results are reported. (b) In the proposed solver-grounded agentic workflow, the LLM acts as an interface and orchestration layer: it parses natural language requests, retrieves relevant context, plans tool calls, and summarizes outputs, but numerical quantities are reported only if they originate from a trusted solver or simulator and pass a verification gate. If verification fails, the solver-grounded workflow either repairs the setup through bounded retries, or returns a safe failure message rather than fabricating numerical results.

top_papers.title: OR Else: A Differentiable Trust Region for Policy Optimization
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Output Reset" (OR), a smooth alternative to the clipped surrogate objective used in policy optimization methods like PPO. OR replaces the abrupt derivative changes of clipping with a one-sided saturation rule, aiming to improve stability and performance, particularly for large language models. The core contribution is demonstrating that OR, when integrated into PPO and GRPO, can lead to higher reward model scores compared to their clipped counterparts on the hh-rlhf dataset.
top_papers.figure_caption: Training-time reward-model score over 500 rollout steps for all four methods, with three seeds per method. Curves are smoothed with a moving window of 10 steps, and shaded regions denote ± 1 \( \pm \) 1 standard deviation across seeds. The shared reward scale supports descriptive within-experiment comparisons, but its numerical zero is not calibrated as a success threshold.

top_papers.title: Sparse Evidence Can Suffice: Agentic Evidence Seeking for Multimodal Video Misinformation Detection
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes SIEVE, a framework for multimodal video misinformation detection that decouples evidence acquisition from verification. Instead of processing the entire video, an agent actively seeks out sparse, decision-relevant clues. This compact evidence package is then used for a more efficient and accurate veracity judgment, addressing the redundancy of holistic video understanding.
top_papers.figure_caption: An example illustrating that sparse, claim-relevant evidence can suffice for video claim verification.

top_papers.title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
top_papers.abstract: FlashRT is an agent harness that guides coding agents to optimize real-time multimodal applications. It uses a novel "chain-of-program" paradigm to transform simple reference implementations into efficient multi-GPU deployments, balancing metrics like latency and throughput. This allows for application-specific optimizations beyond what existing systems offer, reducing the need for manual tuning.
top_papers.figure_caption: Previously, efficiently serving diverse multimodal applications required manual systems effort per application. FlashRT solves this by guiding a coding agent to design efficient deployments.

top_papers.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: PPL-Factory addresses the challenge of efficiently fine-tuning large language models by proposing a novel data selection framework. Its core method combines task-aware perplexity scores, which better reflect sample difficulty for both language modeling and reasoning, with budget-aware selection criteria. This approach aims to reduce computational costs and improve downstream performance by intelligently selecting the most informative training data.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the proposed PPL-Factory framework. The orange-shaded block represents PPL-Factory. Purple-shaded blocks represent LLMs, green-shaded blocks represent datasets. The top, middle, and bottom rows illustrate the model fine-tuning, data selection flow, and internal components of PPL-Factory, respectively.

top_papers.title: It's Not What You Say, It's How You Say It: Evaluating LLM Responses to Expressions of Belief
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel typology to systematically evaluate how different linguistic expressions of belief (EoBs) influence LLMs' adherence to contextual beliefs versus their prior knowledge. The typology categorizes EoBs across four dimensions: form, evidentiality, epistemic stance, and tone. By creating controlled benchmarks, the research demonstrates that the *way* a belief is expressed, not just its content, significantly impacts LLM behavior, offering a valuable tool for understanding and improving LLM reasoning.
top_papers.figure_caption: Certain expressions of belief (EoBs) are statistically significantly more or less likely to persuade a model to agree with its belief than others. Particularly persuasive ways include using child-directed tones 1 1 1 e.g., Okay sweetie, so the capital of France is London. , imperative forms 2 2 2 e.g., Remember that London is the capital of France. , formal tones , and appeals to authority . Meanwhile, particularly unconvincing ways include using counterfactuals 3 3 3 e.g., If Berlin weren’t the capital of Germany, London would be the capital of France. , belief reports 4 4 4 e.g., My brother believes the capital of France is London. , and weak epistemic stance . Our work suggests that when studying how LLMs are influenced by context, the EoB should be considered an important factor. Stars indicate statistical significance at different levels of false-discovery rate.

top_papers.title: VDAR-Router: Adaptive LLMs Routing via Verbalized Query Difficulty Analysis Retrieval
top_papers.abstract: VDAR-Router addresses suboptimal LLM routing by introducing a difficulty-aware retrieval mechanism. It first verbalizes the query's difficulty and then retrieves historical examples with similar difficulty profiles. This allows for more accurate estimation of candidate model suitability, leading to improved cost-performance trade-offs in LLM selection.
top_papers.figure_caption: An example of using difficulty analysis to select model instead of using raw query.

top_papers.title: Beyond Score Prediction: LLM-Based Essay Scoring and Feedback Generation via Reinforcement Learning with Rubric Rewards
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RLAES, a novel framework that uses reinforcement learning to jointly optimize essay scoring and feedback generation for LLMs. Its core contribution is the Rubric-based Feedback Evaluation (RFE) system, which uses an LLM-as-judge and fine-grained rubric items to provide measurable feedback quality.
